tasks.short: Enter and retrieve data for medical records sent to physicians.

steps.what: Read which medical records wait for data entry
Open the retrieval packet for those medical records
Confirm the retrieval packet names this patient
Copy coded results into those medical records
Type narrative findings that still need inclusion
Correct copied results that disagree with the source
Complete transmission of the checked records to physicians

tasks.design: A configured feed copies coded values from the laboratory message into the {OTHER} clinical record once the laboratory has stored them as fields. She still matches the patient, types findings with no field, and reads every copied result before she hands the record to the physician. The clinical applications specialist keeps the field map, and that upkeep is not her time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Laboratory values and referral facts sat in a second store, and she re-keyed them into the medical record.
tasks.enabler_now: A configured feed copies coded fields once the laboratory stores them as values. Free text still has no field.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong patient or a wrong unit can harm someone, so she still reads every copied result.
tasks.human_edge: She notices when a result belongs to a different patient, or when a unit does not match the source packet.
tasks.altitude: She still matches the patient and still reads every copied result before the physician sees the record. She spends less time retyping values that already have a field.

reach.task: Record laboratory results that already arrive as codes.
reach.learn: Which fields the laboratory stores before she opens the record.

evidence.claim: Copying coded laboratory fields into a clinical record is a field map, not a model.
Health data is a special category, and care use of the dossier rests on article 9(2)(h) with professional secrecy.

assumptions: The focal role is the medical transcriptionist at a mid-size European clinic. She does not sign the report.
Coded fields are test code, numeric result, unit, and reference flag. The laboratory or the referring office stores them before she opens the record. She does not capture those fields.
The clinical applications specialist maintains the map from those fields to the clinical record. That is other-role time, not her baseline, and not runtime.
Unmapped narrative stays her typing. Her incremental hours on this task are zero because she does not keep the field map.
Physician time is not in these shares. Handing the checked record to the physician stays her step and is not a second typing.
Time the record already spends storing a row is not her hours.
unknowns: How often the source is a coded laboratory message rather than a paper referral or a free-text letter.
research_questions: What share of a week is coded laboratory messages versus free-text referrals?

already_counted.description: Matching the packet to the patient stays in s3.
Reading copied results back against the source stays in s6.

incremental.description: The clinical applications specialist keeps the field map when a new test code appears. She does not.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a paper-referral day almost every value is still typed, so only a small coded slice drops. On a coded laboratory day the re-key drops and the narrative, the patient match, and the read-back stay. High stays under the re-key share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take dictation with shorthand, a stenotype, or headsets.

steps.what: Load dictation taken by shorthand or a stenotype machine
Listen using headsets on the transcribing machines
Draft that dictation into the report text

loop.input: Dictated audio and the patient header.
loop.output: Draft report text with uncertain spans left blank.
loop.check: Drug names and abbreviations are compared with a fixed list. A span that misses the list is left blank.
loop.stop: Stop when the audio is drafted, or when a low-confidence span is left blank for her to type. No second pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: A plain transcript mangles drug names and accents. A fixed form cannot hear the sentence.

steps.what: Correct wrong drugs and gaps in that draft
Return the corrected dictation for physician signature

tasks.design: A bounded draft turns the dictated audio into report text and leaves a low-confidence span blank. She still listens with the headset and corrects drug names against the audio before the physician sees the text. The clinical applications specialist keeps the drug and abbreviation list. An unsigned draft does not enter the dossier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medical speech, drug names, and accents were too messy for a fixed form, and an unchecked draft could enter the dossier.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft from the audio is feasible, with a fixed drug list. Her listen is still required before anyone signs.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted notes still contain errors. The physician must sign before the dossier keeps the report.
tasks.human_edge: She hears a mumbled drug name and a wrong unit that a draft leaves blank or writes wrongly.
tasks.altitude: She still listens to the dictation and still corrects the draft against the audio. She spends less time typing sentences that were clear.

reach.task: Draft a note from recorded speech and correct the words that matter.
reach.learn: Which term list they trust, and which span they still type.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dragon Copilot lists dictation and ambient notes that a person still edits.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three scribes.
Health data is a special category, and care use of the dossier rests on article 9(2)(h) with professional secrecy.
One hospital keeps only the checked summary and deletes the rest within a day.
A regulator found Class I not compatible for a scribe whose notes feed continued care, and Class IIa is the floor.
Scribe usage logs that measure clinicians need works-council consent and are high-risk.

assumptions: The physician records the audio before this task. That capture is the physician's time, not hers. She loads what is already queued.
The clinical applications specialist maintains the fixed list of drug names and abbreviations. Her incremental hours on this task are zero because she does not keep that list.
Listening and correcting stay her work. The draft does not wait on her check. She returns only the corrected text.
This design does not score her or the physicians. A log of who opened the dossier is not a productivity score.
Physician signature time is not in these shares. An unsigned draft is not written into the dossier.
unknowns: How often the audio is mumbled, or names a drug missing from the fixed list.
research_questions: What share of a dictation day is clear speech versus spans she still types by ear?

already_counted.description: Listening to the dictation with the headset stays in s2.
Correcting drugs and blank spans against the audio stays in s4.

incremental.description: The clinical applications specialist adds a drug name or an abbreviation to the fixed list. She does not.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a mumbled tape she still types the unclear stretches, so only part of the typing drops. On a clear-dictation day most of the typing drops. Listening, correction, and the return for signature stay. High stays under the typing share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Handle clerical mail and complete insurance claims.

steps.what: Sort incoming and outgoing clerical mail
Attach each letter to the matching patient
Read the signed report beside the tariff line
Fill the insurance claims lines from those fields
Check those claims against the signed report
Finish submitting the checked claims to the insurer
Finish filing the office copy of those claims

tasks.design: Claim lines are filled from fields on the signed report and from the tariff the billing specialist already published. She still checks the procedure, the patient, and the amount, and she still submits the claim to the insurer herself. Sorting mail and filing the office copy stay her work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The claim form asked for codes she copied by hand from the signed report and the tariff.
tasks.enabler_now: The signed report and the tariff are both structured, so the lines can be filled without a model.
tasks.still_hard: She still checks the procedure and the amount, and she still sends the claim herself.
tasks.human_edge: She sees when the procedure, the patient, or the amount on the claim does not match the signed report.
tasks.altitude: She still sorts the mail, still checks each claim, and still submits it. She spends less time retyping lines that are already fields.

reach.task: Complete an insurance claim from a signed treatment note.
reach.learn: Which tariff line the billing specialist publishes, and which amount they still check.

evidence.claim: Filling claim lines from coded report fields and a tariff table is a field map and arithmetic, not a model.
Health data placed in an insurance claim is special-category data.

assumptions: This is the clerical slice of a transcription desk: mail, a claim, typing of claim lines, and filing. It is not one invented admin block.
The billing specialist publishes the tariff line. That authorship is other-role time and is not in her baseline.
Her incremental hours on this task are zero because she does not keep the tariff.
Submitting the checked claim is a send she still does. It is not counted as a saving. Filing the office copy stays hers.
Colleague mail stays inside the clinic. Only the insurer send leaves the organisation.
unknowns: Which lawful basis the clinic uses when claim data leave for the insurer.
How often a claim line is a free-text note rather than a code on the signed report.
research_questions: What share of claim lines are codes already on the signed report?

already_counted.description: Checking procedure, patient, and amount against the signed report stays in s5.
Submitting the checked claim to the insurer stays in s6.

incremental.description: The billing specialist keeps the tariff table when a code or an amount changes. She does not.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a day of free-text claim notes she still types most lines. On a day when every line is a code from the signed report, the fill drops. Mail, the check, the insurer send, and filing stay. High stays under the fill share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide what information reports include or exclude.

steps.what: Read the dictation behind these reports
Place the stored headings on that report
Decide which information should be included or excluded
Write the findings she chose to keep
Hand that written report to the physician

tasks.design: The heading list for a report type is stored and placed on the report. She still decides which information is included or excluded, and she still writes the findings she keeps. The medical records lead keeps that heading list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report type had its own headings, and she rebuilt them while deciding what to keep.
tasks.enabler_now: The heading list for a report type can be stored and applied. The include or exclude call stays hers.
tasks.still_hard: A heading does not know which finding matters for this patient. Drafted notes still contain errors, so a model does not make the include or exclude call.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which finding changes the report and which repeated phrase does not belong for this patient.
tasks.altitude: She still decides what the report includes and still writes the findings she keeps. She spends less time rebuilding the same headings.

reach.task: Choose which findings stay in a visit note.
reach.learn: Which headings repeat, and which finding they still decide themselves.

evidence.claim: Applying a stored list of headings for a report type is configuration. It does not decide which finding to keep.
A preprint found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes from three scribes.

assumptions: The medical records lead maintains the heading list for each report type. Her incremental hours on this task are zero because she does not keep that list.
Placing headings does not decide inclusion. She still reads the dictation and writes the findings she keeps.
Handing the written report to the physician stays her step. It is not a saving.
A heading list does not need a model. The prior that a model is needed is not followed here.
unknowns: Which report types already have a heading list the medical records lead maintains.
research_questions: How many report types does she type often enough that the headings repeat?

already_counted.description: Deciding what is included or excluded stays in s3.
Writing the findings she keeps stays in s4.

incremental.description: The medical records lead adds or retires a heading for a report type. She does not.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a rare report type she still types the headings, so little drops. On a familiar report type the skeleton drops and the include or exclude call stays. High stays under the heading share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still matches the patient, still corrects the transcript against the audio, still decides what the report includes, and still submits the claim. She spends less time retyping coded values, clear dictated sentences, and claim lines.
reach: Medical Assistants: which coded results they already store, so those values are not typed again.
Speech-Language Pathology Assistants: which chart headings repeat for a report type, and which finding they still write.
Pharmacy Aides: which drug names on a fixed list are safe to flag, and which name they still check by ear.
skills_to_grow: Match a source packet to the patient before any value is copied.
Correct a drug name or a blank span against the audio.
Decide which finding stays in the report.
role.ambitious_version: On a morning of clear dictation and coded laboratory messages, the draft text and the copied results are waiting. She still listens, still corrects the drugs, still decides what the report keeps, and still sends the claim herself.
